title: High average well-being and social cohesion coexist with unequal participation, mental-health pressure, and a reliability crisis in government
source_unit: Sociaal en Cultureel Planbureau, Sociale en Culturele Ontwikkelingen 2026
geography: The Netherlands, with European comparisons using European Social Survey round 11 (2023)

denominator.unit: SCP Netherlands in Beeld aggregate survey and European comparison frame

life_satisfaction.unit: average life-satisfaction score reported by SCP

paid_work.unit: percent of people with paid work in 2024/2025

overall_direction.value: average well-being, participation, and social trust are broadly high or stable, while large group differences remain

measurement_frame.value: quality of life, social cohesion, and the relationship between citizens and government are assessed together

observations.method: SCP synthesis of the Netherlands in Beeld continuous survey, historical comparisons, European Social Survey round 11 comparisons, and expert interpretation across quality of life, social cohesion, and citizen-government relations.
observations.uncertainty: National averages can conceal subgroup, neighborhood, age, income, and education differences; the report is an assessment framework and monitoring publication, not a causal model of well-being.
observations.subgroup: Residents grouped by income and educational attainment, younger people and young adults, caregivers, workers, volunteers, and people with different experiences of government.
observations.counterinterpretation: High average well-being and participation are real resources; the report identifies distributional and institutional vulnerabilities rather than declaring society to be in generalized decline.

observations.period: 2024-2026; income and education gradients in social trust and life satisfaction

denominator.unit: SCP subgroup comparison frame from Netherlands in Beeld

trust_by_income.value: 50% of the lowest-income group say other people can be trusted, compared with 60% of the middle-income group and 68% of the highest-income group

life_satisfaction_by_income.value: life satisfaction is 78% among the lowest-income group, 86% among the middle-income group, and 92% among the highest-income group

trust_by_education.value: 47% of the bo/vmbo education group, 56% of the havo/vwo/mbo group, and 73% of the hbo/wo group say other people can be trusted

satisfaction_by_education.value: life satisfaction is 82%, 85%, and 91% across those three education groups

observations.method: SCP subgroup comparisons of survey-based social trust and life satisfaction, split by income and educational attainment.
observations.uncertainty: These are reported subgroup associations from survey measures; they do not isolate income or education as the sole cause and do not describe every dimension of inequality.
observations.subgroup: Lowest, middle, and highest income groups; bo/vmbo, havo/vwo/mbo, and hbo/wo educational groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: The gradients coexist with high satisfaction in every group and may reflect multiple linked resources, health, security, networks, and institutional experiences rather than a single deficit.

observations.period: 2024-2026; health, care, participation, and social cohesion

mental_health_youth.value: 66% of participants aged 18-25 are above the threshold for mental-health complaints, compared with 52% among ages 26-65

experienced_health.unit: percent reporting their health as good or very good

healthy_life_years.value: the number of healthy life years has declined in recent years and the Netherlands has fallen in the European ranking over the past two decades
healthy_life_years.unit: SCP synthesis citing national and European indicators

cohesion_boundary.value: social cohesion is high in European comparison but differs substantially between groups and neighborhoods

observations.method: SCP synthesis of survey-based well-being, mental-health, health-status, care, participation, neighborhood-cohesion, and European comparison indicators.
observations.uncertainty: The indicators use different sources and time frames; the threshold measure is not a clinical diagnosis and the report does not establish a single cause of mental-health or healthy-life-year changes.
observations.subgroup: Young people and young adults, working-age adults, caregivers, people with different income and education levels, and residents of different neighborhoods.
observations.counterinterpretation: Strong cohesion and high self-rated health provide resilience and a platform for targeted support; attention to pressure points need not negate the broader positive baseline.

denominator.unit: SCP Netherlands in Beeld and European parliament-trust comparison frame

parliament_trust.unit: average score out of 10 for trust in the Dutch House of Representatives

problem_solving_trust.unit: average score for confidence that government can solve problems

institutional_assessment.value: citizens report low political trust, low perceived responsiveness, weak confidence in problem-solving, and concerns about procedural fairness

legitimacy_boundary.value: government legitimacy is not broadly rejected, but persistent low trust may become a longer-run legitimacy risk

observations.method: SCP survey indicators and European comparisons of parliamentary trust, responsiveness, procedural justice, legitimacy, and perceived problem-solving, interpreted alongside longer-run institutional experience.
observations.uncertainty: Trust scores are perceptions and do not directly measure institutional performance or predict political behavior; the report identifies a risk pathway rather than a causal forecast.
observations.subgroup: Residents across income and education groups, with generally low trust across groups and modest differences between them.
observations.counterinterpretation: Critical citizens can still support democratic institutions; low trust may reflect demands for reliability and accountability rather than immediate rejection of government legitimacy.

related_sources.claim: SCP methodological appendix for the Netherlands in Beeld measures and subgroup comparisons.
English-language institutional context for the Netherlands Institute for Social Research.

boundary: This record adds a national public-sector social-condition route across well-being, participation, social trust, mental-health pressure, inequality, and citizen-government reliability. It uses published aggregate and subgroup survey results plus European comparisons, not raw respondent-level data, clinical diagnoses, individual political histories, causal policy evaluation, or a claim that Dutch results generalize to every country.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official SCP publication page and PDF reviewed for the analytical framework, life satisfaction, paid work, income and education gradients, mental-health comparison, health, social cohesion, political trust, and problem-solving indicators.
